messages:
maria: Heads-up — SIEM alert: sudden spike in KMS Decrypt failures from svc-ingest across multiple hosts in us-west-2. Not tied to deployments in the logs I can see. Threshold hit ~350/min. Thoughts?

devon: thanks, digging quick. are these 401/AccessDenied or retries?

maria: most are `AccessDenied` with `principalId: svc-ingest@redwood-prod`. A few show `AccessDenied: KMS key not found` (weird).

aj: paste the query you're using?

maria: here —
```
index=siem logs | where event.action == "kms:Decrypt" and region=="us-west-2" | stats count() by outcome, src_service, key_id
```

olivia: could be deployment that rotated key alias or a transient permission change during a rollout. Any RBAC/iam policy changes in last 2 hours? @ryan fyi

ryan: no IAM changes in that window from infra side. We did a config push to ingest last night but nothing targeting KMS.

sre-ops: I'm seeing increased retries from the same container image sha: `ingest:v2026.03.19-9a2b`. CPU spike earlier but nothing huge.

devon: two quick hypotheses — 1) service account temporarily lost kms:Decrypt via role binding change, 2) KMS key got re-created (rotation script bug) so key id changed while alias remained, causing some older hosts to reference old key id.

maria: agree. Want to avoid a noisy alert flood while we triage. Can we tune the rule to suppress repeated failures from the same principal within a short window (i.e., collapse to one incident / minute), and add an enrichment for `deploy.sha` so we can see correlation?

aj: +1 on enrichment. For suppression pattern we can use a sliding window and require >X distinct principals or >Y unique key_ids to trigger. Current rule is just count>100/min which catches retries.

sec-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0319-27 (auto). Pager escalation suppressed because alert group contains >90% same principal.

olivia: action items: 1) add `deploy.sha` and `host.instance_id` to SIEM ingestion (low effort), 2) change rule to `count(distinct key_id) > 3 OR count(distinct principalId) > 10` OR `count(total) > 500` to avoid retry storms. Anyone object?

ryan: sounds good. For temporary relief we can mute the current alert for 30m while we roll the rule.

devon: I'll propose the query change and put a PR for the rule in #siem-rules. Suggested rule snippet: 
```
when (
  distinct_count(key_id) > 3 or
  distinct_count(principalId) > 10 or
  total_count > 500
) then alert
else suppress
```

maria: also please add a heuristic to ignore `AccessDenied` when `user.agent == "kms-rotation-job"` — that's a known maintenance pattern.

aj: noted. Also adding anomaly enrichment: reverse-DNS for src IP and a tag for `service_tier` so we can suppress dev/test traffic # if it leaks.

sre-ops: muted alert for 30m now.

maria: quick validation: after enrichment change can we re-run the historical query (last 24h) to sanity-check FP rate? I want to make sure we don't hide a real incident.

devon: yes — will run backfill and post a small chart here.

sec-bot: backfill job queued: backfill-176345. ETA ~4m.

ryan: remote hosts with older key ids: we found 6 hosts that still reference `key-abc123` which was rotated at 2026-03-19T02:14Z. Those hosts are on the earlier image — seems rollout staggered.

maria: ok that matches hypothesis. Plan: patch rule + enrichment now, mute 30m, run backfill, open follow-up ticket to ensure rotation job not leaving stale references (assigned to infra).

olivia: assigning follow-up ticket under INFRA-1427 for key rotation cleanup.

aj: PR posted for rule change: https://git.internal/redwood/siem-rules/pull/482 (includes tests and backfill query).

devon: backfill shows 85% of failures map to those 6 hosts and old key id. After grouping by instance_id, alerts would have collapsed to 6 noisy sources rather than global flood.

maria: good. once PR is merged we'll unmute and monitor. thanks all :thumbsup:

ryan: FYI I'll schedule a small maintenance to re-bootstrap those hosts.

sre-ops: unmute scheduled after PR merge and deploy.

maria: closing for now — will reopen if pattern persists. Follow-up: INFRA-1427 (rotation cleanup) and SIEM-483 (rule rollout verification).
